events.title: The death of St. Aldegundis of Maubeuge
events.shortBlurb: The Merovingian princess who founded the double monastery of Maubeuge and bore slander and cancer without complaint died on 30 January…
body: Aldegundis was born about 639 in Hainault, daughter of Walbert and Bertilia, of the kindred of the Merovingian kings, and sister of St. Waldetrudis of Mons. Consecrating herself to God in her youth, she resisted every suit of marriage and received the veil from St. Amandus, bishop of Maastricht; then, about 661, she founded on the banks of the Sambre the abbey of Maubeuge, a house of nuns which she governed as its first abbess.

Her life was a hidden one of prayer, tried by violent slanders and, at the end, by a lingering cancer of the breast, whose tortures — the caustics and incisions of the surgeons — she bore, Butler says, not only with patience but with joy.

She died on 30 January, in 684 as most modern accounts reckon, though Butler, following the Bollandists, gives 660. Her relics were enshrined at Maubeuge; her name stands on this day in the martyrologies of Rabanus Maurus, Usuard, and Notker, and in the Roman Martyrology; and she is invoked as a patroness of those who suffer from cancer.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 30 January
